name: connector_sources
description:
List the company databases declared on the stand: each source's name, engine (mongodb, sqlserver or postgresql), database, the collections
an agent may read and what a person wrote about it. Start here, then read a source's shape with connector_schema.

name: connector_schema
description:
Read what a source holds before querying it. Without a collection: the collections or tables an agent may read.
With one: for MongoDB, its fields read from a sample of 200 documents — each field's dotted path, its types, how
often it is present and an example value; for SQL, its columns with their types and an example value. Both answer
how many rows it holds and its indexes, which are what a query is quick on.

source.description: The source's name, as connector_sources lists it.

collection.description: The collection whose fields to read; without one, the collections an agent may read.

name: connector_find
description:
Read documents of a collection that match a filter, with the fields and order asked for. Write the filter,
projection and sort as MongoDB Extended JSON, such as {"status": "paid", "total": {"$gt": 100}}; dates as {"$date": "2026-01-31T00:00:00Z"}, ids as {"$oid": "…"}. An answer carries 50 documents unless asked for more, at most 200, and at
most 65536 bytes of them; when it was cut it says so — narrow the filter or count first. A query gets 30 seconds.
Only reads: operators that write or run code are refused.

source.description: The source's name, as connector_sources lists it.

collection.description: The collection, as connector_schema lists it.

filter.description: Which documents, as MongoDB Extended JSON, such as {"status": "paid", "total": {"$gt": 100}}; dates as {"$date": "2026-01-31T00:00:00Z"}, ids as {"$oid": "…"}; empty matches every one.

projection.description: Which fields to return, such as {"number": 1, "total": 1, "_id": 0}; empty returns them all.

sort.description: The order, such as {"date": -1}; empty leaves the database's order.

limit.description: How many rows to return: 50 when not given, at most 200.

name: connector_aggregate
description:
Run a MongoDB aggregation pipeline on a collection to group, sum, count and join — the way to analyse rather than
list. Write the pipeline as a JSON array of stages in MongoDB Extended JSON, such as {"status": "paid", "total": {"$gt": 100}}; dates as {"$date": "2026-01-31T00:00:00Z"}, ids as {"$oid": "…"}. $lookup, $graphLookup and $unionWith may
read only collections the source allows; $out, $merge, $function, $accumulator and $where are refused. The answer
carries 50 rows unless asked for more, at most 200, at most 65536 bytes; a query gets 30 seconds.

source.description: The source's name, as connector_sources lists it.

collection.description: The collection, as connector_schema lists it.

pipeline.description: The stages as a JSON array, such as [{"$match": {"status": "paid"}}, {"$group": {"_id": "$customer", "total": {"$sum": "$total"}}}].

limit.description: How many rows to return: 50 when not given, at most 200.

name: connector_count
description:
Count the documents of a collection that match a filter, written as MongoDB Extended JSON, such as {"status": "paid", "total": {"$gt": 100}}; dates as {"$date": "2026-01-31T00:00:00Z"}, ids as {"$oid": "…"}; an empty filter counts them
all. Cheaper than reading them: count before reading a large collection.

source.description: The source's name, as connector_sources lists it.

collection.description: The collection, as connector_schema lists it.

filter.description: Which documents, as MongoDB Extended JSON, such as {"status": "paid", "total": {"$gt": 100}}; dates as {"$date": "2026-01-31T00:00:00Z"}, ids as {"$oid": "…"}; empty matches every one.

name: connector_query
description:
Run one SELECT on a SQL source — PostgreSQL or SQL Server — to search, join, group and sum. The statement is a
SELECT or a WITH ending in one; anything that writes or changes the database is refused, and it runs as the
read-only user in a transaction that is rolled back. Tables after FROM and JOIN must be ones the source allows.
The answer carries 50 rows unless asked for more, at most 200, at most 65536 bytes; a query gets 30 seconds.
For MongoDB sources use connector_find and connector_aggregate.

source.description: The source's name, as connector_sources lists it.

select.description: The SELECT, such as SELECT c.city, sum(o.total) FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.city.

limit.description: How many rows to return: 50 when not given, at most 200.

name: connector_export
description:
Write rows into a csv or xlsx file of the task, under exports/ of the working copy, which the task's card offers a
person to download. For MongoDB, give a collection and either a filter or a pipeline; nested fields become columns
of their dotted paths. For SQL, give a select. An export writes at most 100000 rows and says when it stopped there,
and at most 1000 columns: the fields past them go into one column, _more, as JSON. The answer comes once the file
is written; an export still writing when the wait runs out answers with its job, job://connector/export/<id>,
whose resource carries the same answer once the file is there.

source.description: The source's name, as connector_sources lists it.

format.description: The file's format: csv or xlsx.

file.description: The file's name, letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores; the format's extension is added when missing.

collection.description: For MongoDB, the collection, as connector_schema lists it; not used for SQL.

filter.description: Which documents, as MongoDB Extended JSON, such as {"status": "paid", "total": {"$gt": 100}}; dates as {"$date": "2026-01-31T00:00:00Z"}, ids as {"$oid": "…"}; empty matches every one.

pipeline.description: For MongoDB, the stages as a JSON array, when the rows come from a pipeline rather than a filter.

select.description: For SQL, the SELECT whose rows the file holds; not used for MongoDB.

wait.description: Seconds to wait for the file before answering with the export's job; 60 when not given, 0 answers with the job at once, at most 900.

name: connector_journal
description:
Read the queries this task already made — which source and collection, what was asked, how many rows came back,
whether it failed — newest first, so a query is not repeated. Every query is written there, for the company to see.

most.description: How many queries to return, newest first: at most 200.

name: connector_propose_write
description:
Propose a change to a company database — update, update_one, insert or delete — when the task needs one. Nothing is written: the server
dry-runs it as the read-only user, counts the documents it touches and keeps a few of them as they are now, and
answers a proposal id. Then call request_write_approval with server "connector" and that proposal: the task waits
until the stand's owner or an administrator reads the proposal and allows or refuses it. An update or a delete needs a filter naming
the documents; an update is field operators such as $set; one proposal touches at most 1000 documents or rows.
The source must have a writing user. On a SQL source the collection is the table, the filter is columns and
values — {"id": 42}, or comparisons $eq, $ne, $gt, $gte, $lt, $lte, $in and $null, all of which must hold — an
update is $set and $inc, an insert is an array of rows, and update_one needs a filter that matches exactly one
row; the server writes the statement itself.

source.description: The source's name, as connector_sources lists it.

collection.description: The collection, as connector_schema lists it.

operation.description: What the write does: update, update_one, insert or delete.

reason.description: Why the task needs this write, in one or two sentences for the person who decides.

filter.description: Which documents or rows an update or a delete touches, such as {"number": "2026-0042"}, or on SQL {"id": 42, "due": {"$lt": "2026-06-01"}}; it may not be empty. Not used by an insert.

change.description: For an update, the field operators, such as {"$set": {"status": "paid"}} (on SQL only $set and $inc); for an insert, a JSON array of the documents or rows; not used by a delete.

name: connector_apply
description:
Run a proposal the stand's owner or an administrator allowed, once, as the source's writing user, and get back how many documents or
rows it changed. Only the task that proposed it may run it, once, and only within 7 days; a proposal nobody allowed
yet, refused, already run or being run is refused with what to do. On SQL it runs in one transaction, rolled back
when it would touch more rows than the person allowed.

name: connector_diagnose
description: Say whether the server can reach the stand's sources: its version, Vault, and how many sources are declared. Changes nothing.
